title: ALMOST HUMAN
subtitle: Unfinished gestures — collar adjustments, wrist checks, and doorway hesitations
lineage: Primary: SCION 057 (Moments) · Supporting: SCION 084 (Pickpocket), SCION 085 (Jeanne Dielman)
theorem: Make a sequence from six situated gesture excerpts: begin with one complete collar adjustment including the pause afterward; let another person begin a similar movement with a different outcome; build a rhythm across three gestures before one stops halfway; return to the first setting.
boundary_note: The comparison concerns visible actions and preserves source circumstances rather than inferring identical motives or a universal account of humanity.

v1_defect_timecodes: Seg #04 (t=17.00s-23.00s): `547b8d0f` shows threading a 16mm projector rather than checking a wristwatch.
Seg #05 (t=23.00s-28.50s): `af625567` at in_s=0.5s crosses an internal cut at 2.79s before the wristwatch close-up.
Seg #06 (t=28.50s-34.50s): `dd216185` crosses an internal cut at 3.8s from the woman on the stairs to a boy at a closet.
critic_tribunal.largest_gap: Seg #04 shows projector threading instead of a wristwatch check, while Seg #05 and Seg #06 cross internal cuts mid-gesture.
critic_tribunal.causal_hypothesis: OpenCLIP false positive on `547b8d0f`, and unclamped cut boundaries in `af625567` (cut at 2.79s) and `dd216185` (cut at 3.80s).
critic_tribunal.falsifiable_repair: Use `af625567` clamped to its verified wristwatch close-up window (`2.85s-6.00s`) for Seg #04, paired with verified hourglass time-check `7aa7b9d2` (`18.0s-23.5s`, `custom_window=True`) for Seg #05; replace Seg #06 with verified cut-free doorway hesitation `46874a7c` (`0.2s-6.2s`, 8.3s clean window).
critic_tribunal.strength_to_preserve: The opening complete collar adjustment in `9d763244` (`Basic Typing`, 1944), contrasting fabric touch in `e76fd644`, stopping halfway in `9c590333`, and returning to `9d763244` after the gesture.
